newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds barely move, lacking incentives.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds barely move, lacking incentives.

text.p: *Australian bonds barely moved in early trading, finding few fresh incentives in front of next week's RBA board meeting.
*Thursday's retail trade seen as only key local event.
*U.S. releases several major indicators this week.
Australian bonds got off to a slow start to the week, barely moving from Friday's closing levels in the absence of few fresh incentives in front of next week's Reserve Bank board meeting.

A 50 basis point easing in monetary policy is largely factored in, as it has been more or less for over a month, and until such a move is endorsed by the RBA the market will find it difficult to progress last week's rally further.
The 10-year bond futures contract struck an all-time high of 93.640 last week, which took the cash yield below 6.40 percent, its lowest level since the early 1980s.
Thursday's retail trade data is seen as the only local indicator of importance this week, although it is unlikely to change the market's view that an interest rate cut is on the agenda, traders said.
The June balance of goods and services and building approvals are also due on Tuesday and Wednesday respectively.

The driving force for the market is otherwise likely to come from U.S., where a steady flow of data includes the second quarter employment cost index on Tuesday, the advanced GDP reading for the same quarter on Thursday and the all important July non-farm payrolls on Friday.

Yield spreads to the U.S. were little changed, while they tightened to the Canadian short end where the Canadian currency came under pressure. U.S. yields crept higher on Friday during a tightly traded session. New Zealand debt also remained hostage to the plight of the N.Z. dollar.
